aggressive_definition_excerpt: Regarding prostate cancer aggressiveness, the 677TT genotype was associated with more than 50% decreased risk of high-grade prostate cancer (Gleason score >7) compared with the 677CC and 677CT genotypes (OR = 0.35, 95% CI = 0.24-0.64; P = 0.001).
grading_caveat: None; the abstract explicitly labels the endpoint high-grade and defines it as Gleason score >7.
reason: The abstract analyzes general prostate cancer and an explicit high-grade incident endpoint, but the high-grade analysis concerns the MTHFR 677TT genotype rather than folate or vitamin B12 levels.

exposures.supporting_excerpt: Regarding prostate cancer aggressiveness, the 677TT genotype was associated with more than 50% decreased risk of high-grade prostate cancer (Gleason score >7) compared with the 677CC and 677CT genotypes (OR = 0.35, 95% CI = 0.24-0.64; P = 0.001). There was no significant difference in plasma levels of tHcy, folate, and vitamin B12 between the two groups with any genotypes.
exposures.reason: The aggressive association is reported only for the 677TT genotype. Folate levels are compared only between the overall case and control groups, with no high-grade folate analysis established.
